key_decisions.decision: Repeats the emphatic divine subject and ascent/descent; renders the hand-on-eyes death idiom without restricting the return promise to one fulfillment.
Preserves six names and the specific maternal ethnicity attached only to Shaul.
Follows this source’s Job rather than harmonizing to Jashub in other family records; preserves source order.
Makes the group heading inclusive of grandchildren while retaining Dinah, the place, and the source total without silently repairing its counting difficulty.
Separates Serah’s explicit sister relationship from the sons and preserves Beriah’s further generation.
Retains Zilpah’s being given to Leah and counts descendants rather than implying she personally bore sixteen immediate children.
Preserves all ten names as sons here without harmonizing their relationships or forms to later biblical genealogies.
Renders the plural genealogical heading naturally for its one named member without inventing further sons.
Retains Bilhah’s being given and her maternal line’s seven-person total without confusing grandchildren with direct births.
Preserves bodily descent and the explicit exclusion of wives; does not recalculate the Hebrew total.
Retains both the two already born in Egypt and the seventy-person household total, leaving the collective migration wording intact.
Retains the ahead/before movement and destination while allowing the arrival clause to lead into the reunion; the arranging sense of instruct/direct is noted.
Keeps deferential servants distinct from later purchased slaves, ancestral continuity, and the source’s strong abomination language attributed to Egyptians.
